**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0795), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Why would an organisation consider building its own software even when it is cheaper to buy one? (2 marks)

(b) What is the purpose of the system development life cycle (SDLC)? (2 marks)

(c) What is the difference between the pilot implementation methodology and the parallel implementation methodology? (2 marks)

(d) State and describe **two** objectives of the design phase of the SDLC. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Why build its own software (2 marks)**

Any two of:

- **Tailor-made to its needs:** bought (off-the-shelf) software is general and may not do exactly what the organisation does or may need many changes, while custom software meets its requirements exactly.
- **Control:** the organisation owns the software and decides when and how to change, extend and maintain it (new features, updates), without depending on a vendor.
- **Compatibility and integration** with its existing systems and data, and a possible **competitive advantage** (a unique system that competitors cannot buy).
- **Security and no licence fees:** the code is known and under its control, and there are no recurring licence costs.

**(b) Purpose of the SDLC (2 marks)**

The SDLC gives a **structured framework of stages** (for example feasibility study, analysis, design, implementation/coding, testing, installation, maintenance) for **planning, building, delivering and maintaining an information system** so that it meets the users' requirements, is of good quality, and is finished on time and within the budget. It makes the work organised, controlled and documented.

**(c) Pilot and parallel implementation (2 marks)**

- In **pilot** implementation the new system is installed and used **in only one part** of the organisation (one branch, department or group of users) first. If it works well, it is then extended to the rest of the organisation; the other parts keep the old system meanwhile.
- In **parallel** implementation the new system and the old system are **both run at the same time, on the same data, in the whole organisation** for a period; the results are compared, and the old system is stopped only when the new one is shown to work correctly.

**(d) Two objectives of the design phase (4 marks, 2 marks each: statement + description)**

Any two of:

1. **To produce a detailed design of the system that meets the requirements found in the analysis.** The design specifies the processes (algorithms, flowcharts), the data (files, database tables, data dictionary), and the inputs and outputs.
2. **To design the user interface** (input forms, screens, reports and menus) so that the system is easy and pleasant to use and the data entered is checked (validation).
3. **To specify the hardware, software and network required** by the system, and to estimate the cost, so that the system can be bought or built.
4. **To plan the testing, security and implementation** of the system (test plan with test data, backup and access rights), so that it can be coded and checked against the design.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) State **two** ways through which confidentiality of information can be achieved. (2 marks)

(b) Give an example of a scenario where availability can be compromised. (2 marks)

(c) State **three** characteristics of information that make it useful for decision-making. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Two ways of achieving confidentiality (2 marks, 1 mark each)**

Any two of:

- **Encryption** of the data (stored or sent), so that only people with the key can read it;
- **Passwords and authentication** (user names, PINs, biometrics) with **access rights** (permissions) that limit who can see which data;
- physical security (locked rooms, badges), a **firewall**, and the secure destruction of printed or stored data that is no longer needed.

**(b) Scenario where availability is compromised (2 marks)**

*Example:* a **denial-of-service (DoS) attack** floods the web server of an online bank with requests, so that customers cannot log in to their accounts. Other acceptable scenarios: a power cut or hardware failure of the server of a school's results system on the day the results are published, or ransomware that locks the files of a hospital.

**(c) Three characteristics of useful information (3 marks, 1 mark each)**

Any three of: **accurate** (free from errors), **timely** (available when it is needed, up to date), **relevant** (suited to the decision to be taken), **complete** (contains everything needed), **reliable** (from a trusted source), **understandable** (clear, presented in a suitable form) and **cost-effective** (the benefit is greater than the cost of obtaining it).
